version.changelog: Security hardening: workspace-scoped file path safety guards, explicit --allow-unsafe-paths override, docs metadata updates, and test file removed from distributed bundle.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: notion-sync
Version: 2.5.2

The notion-sync skill bundle is a legitimate productivity tool for managing Notion workspaces. It demonstrates high security awareness by implementing a 'Path Safety Mode' in `notion-utils.js` to prevent directory traversal and restricting file operations to the current workspace unless explicitly overridden. Credential handling is also handled securely, prioritizing file-based or environment-based tokens over command-line arguments to avoid exposure in process listings. The code uses only built-in Node.js modules, contains no external dependencies, and shows no signs of data exfiltration or malicious execution.

llm.summary: The skill's requests, files, and runtime instructions align with a Notion sync utility: it needs Node and a Notion token, and its scripts only talk to api.notion.com and the local filesystem as documented.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Notion sync) match the included scripts and declared requirements. Required binary (node) and required env var (NOTION_API_KEY) are appropriate and expected for Notion API interactions. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts direct the agent to read/write local files (within workspace by default), read a token from ~/.notion-token, stdin, or NOTION_API_KEY, and call Notion endpoints. This stays within the stated purpose. Note: --allow-unsafe-paths bypasses workspace restrictions and scripts write a workspace-local state file (memory/notion-watch-state.json) by default — these behaviors are documented but grant broader file access if explicitly enabled.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No download/install spec; the skill is shipped with Node scripts and relies on the local node binary. No external archives or URLs are fetched at install time, lowering supply-chain risk. All network calls observed are to the Notion API (api.notion.com).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only NOTION_API_KEY is required (plus optional token-file or stdin). No extra unrelated secrets or environment variables are requested. The token sources and priority are documented in code (token file, stdin, ~/.notion-token, env var).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal model invocation settings. The skill writes its own state file under the workspace (memory/...), but it does not request system-wide or other-skill privileges. Autonomous invocation is permitted (platform default) but is not combined with other concerning privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: Node scripts that call the official Notion API and read/write local files in a documented way. Before installing: 1) Only supply a Notion integration token with the minimum permissions and share only pages/databases the integration needs. 2) Be aware the scripts will auto-read ~/.notion-token if present and may read stdin when requested — don't leave sensitive tokens in world-readable files. 3) The default file-safety mode restricts reads/writes to the current workspace; only use --allow-unsafe-paths if you understand the risk. 4) The skill can be invoked autonomously by the agent (platform default); if you do not want the agent to access your Notion workspace without review, do not enable autonomous use. 5) The bundle references a GitHub repository; if provenance matters, review the upstream repo/commits to confirm authorship and check for recent changes before use.
